title: Student protesters, unions, and the yellow vests hold another nationwide protest in France, with over 100,000 participants.
titleLines: STUDENT PROTESTERS, UNIONS, AND THE YELLOW VESTS HOLD ANOTHER
NATIONWIDE PROTEST IN FRANCE, WITH OVER 100,000 PARTICIPANTS.
subtitle: The role of student activism and labor movements in shaping public opinion and policy in France

logline: Student protesters, unions, and the yellow vests hold another nationwide protest in France, with over 100,000 participants.. This event demonstrates the power of collective action and the intersection of student protests with broader labor

style.look: one sodium lamp against wet black, hard pools of light, rain on stone, faces never shown
rules: Show the object before the explanation: the page, the register, the lamp, the gate.
No bodies, no blood, no reconstruction of violence. The aftermath carries it.
One idea per shot. The camera pushes, reveals or holds; it never drifts.
Cut on the voice. Do not park on a plate after the narration has stopped.
Every number is an official figure or explicitly attributed to a source.

scenes.purpose: Open on one thing the film can hold, then land the title without a lecture.

narration.text: Yellow vests have attacked journalists.
narration.quote: Multiple verbal and physical attacks perpetrated by yellow vests against journalists have been reported and documented throughout the movement.

narration.text: In Toulouse, a reporter was threatened with rape.
narration.quote: The same day, a reporter for the local newspaper La Dépêche du Midi was threatened by yellow vest protesters in Toulouse who told her "we'll take you out of your car and rape you".

narration.text: Police and journalists were assaulted in Lyon.
narration.quote: Ten police officers sustained minor injuries, whilst journalists in Lyon were "assaulted", the ministry said, noting that at least one suspected perpetrator of these assaults has already been arrested.

narration.text: A person was wounded during the protests.
narration.quote: One person was wounded, according to a journalist on the scene.

narration.text: Haute couture is legally protected in France.
narration.quote: The expression Haute couture is, in France, a legally protected name, guaranteeing certain quality standards.

scenes.title: The order
scenes.purpose: Show the decision, who made it, and the words it was made in.

narration.text: The government warned of police using weapons to combat violence.
narration.quote: The day before the Act XII protests, the government warned the public that police would not hesitate to use weapons to combat violence by demonstrators, since they had been authorized by the court.

narration.text: CRS agents were authorized to carry semi-automatic weapons.
narration.quote: Citing 5 January attack on the Dijon gendarmerie and terror threats, the police communication service said that some CRS agents were authorized to carry semi-automatic weapons.

narration.text: Colles are seen as stressful due to high teacher expectations.
narration.quote: Colles are regarded as very stressful, particularly due to the high standards expected by the teachers, and the subsequent harshness that may be directed at students who do not perform adequately.

narration.text: France has 105 international schools as of January 2015.
narration.quote: Most of these schools provide religious instruction in parallel with a broad curriculum. == International education == As of January 2015, the International Schools Consultancy (ISC) listed France as having 105 international schools.

narration.text: Jules Ferry required all children aged 6-12 to attend school.
narration.quote: Jules Ferry, the Minister of Public Instruction in 1881, is widely credited for creating the modern school (l'école républicaine) by requiring all children between the ages of 6 and 12, both boys and girls, to attend.

scenes.purpose: Explain how the decision reached ordinary life: the law, the police, the press.

narration.text: France's highest court denied a request to ban police from using 'flash balls' or 'defensive ball launchers', known as LBDs.
narration.quote: Earlier in the week, France's highest court denied a request to ban police from using "flash balls" or "defensive ball launchers", known as LBDs, that shoot 40 millimetres (1.6 in) rubber projectiles, which have been blamed for a number of serious injuries.

narration.text: French police have made extensive use of tear gas during protests, sometimes causing grievous injuries.
narration.quote: 14/11/2026 - 12:08 'Ten times more painful': Menstrual disorders fuel calls to ban tear gas at French protests French police have made extensive use of tear gas during protests that have roiled France in recent weeks, sometimes causing grievous injuries.

narration.text: In Lille, 20 protesters were arrested after marching between 1,800 and 3,000 people.
narration.quote: Two police officers were injured and two protesters arrested in Morlaix; two officers injured and one demonstrator arrested in Nantes; and in Lille, where between 1,800 and 3,000 protesters marched, 20 were arrested.

narration.text: Tamara Lich, who organized an early yellow vest protest in Medicine Hat, was later arrested for alleged mischief.
narration.quote: An early yellow vest protest, which included "hundreds of vehicles", was held in Medicine Hat, Alberta, organized by Tamara Lich, who was later arrested for alleged mischief pertaining to the 2022 convoy protest in Ottawa.

narration.text: Overall, at least 220 people were arrested in the country, including 142 in Paris.
narration.quote: Overall, at least 220 people were arrested in the country, including 142 in Paris.

narration.quote: On 6 December, over 140 students were arrested outside a school in Mantes-la-Jolie.

narration.text: Thousands in Paris participated in a 'march of the injured' calling for tear gas to be banned.
narration.quote: On Saturday, thousands in Paris participated in a "march of the injured" calling for the weapon to be banned.

narration.text: The man leading insults against a philosopher was detained for questioning on hate speech charges.
narration.quote: The man leading the insults against the philosopher on published video-recordings of the event was detained for questioning on Tuesday on charges of hate speech.

narration.text: 200 people were taken into custody in Paris after the Champs-Elysées was targeted by rioters.
narration.quote: 200 people were taken into custody in Paris after the Champs-Elysées was again targeted by rioters.

narration.text: Versailles Palace was preventively closed for the day.
narration.quote: Versailles Palace was preventively closed for the day. Éric Drouet, the 33-year-old truck driver who is one of the most followed yellow jackets on Facebook, was arrested for organizing an undeclared demonstration and participating in a violent assembly.

scenes.purpose: Find the moment the order broke: the election, the release, the first page printed again.

narration.text: Many protesters had not voted for Macron in 2017.
narration.quote: According to one poll, few of those protesting had voted for Macron in the 2017 presidential election; many had shown political alienation by not voting, or had voted for far-right or far-left candidates.

narration.text: Turnout in recent police union elections was exceptionally high.
narration.quote: Nicolas Chapuis, writing for Le Monde, says this was likely due to 85% turnout in recent police union elections and the exceptional levels of activity.

narration.text: Macron lost his parliamentary majority two months later.
narration.quote: Two months later in the legislative elections, Macron lost his parliamentary majority and had to form a minority government.

narration.text: In the 2022 presidential election, LREM faced a growing far-right party.
narration.quote: LREM's opponent in the second round of the 2017 and 2022 presidential elections was the growing far-right party National Rally (RN).

narration.text: Polls project Melenchon finishing second in next year's election.
narration.quote: Polls also project hard-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon finishing second in next year's election, while the centre-right has struggled to field a single strong contender.

scenes.title: The argument
scenes.purpose: Put the dispute on the table: who defended it, who fought it, and on what ground.

narration.text: The protesters criticized Édouard Philippe's government for the carbon tax burden.
narration.quote: Though allegedly pro-climate, the protesters criticized Édouard Philippe's second government for burdening households with the bulk of the carbon tax, while offering exemptions to many carbon-intensive companies.

narration.text: The yellow vests movement was seen as a populist, grassroots economic justice protest.
narration.quote: The yellow vests movement has been described as a populist, grassroots movement for economic justice, which opposed what it perceived as the wealthy urban elite and the establishment.

narration.text: In February 2019, a truck convoy attracted Yellow Vest participants to Parliament Hill in Ottawa.
narration.quote: A controversial event in February 2019 known as the "United We Roll" truck convoy attracted several Yellow Vest participants to the grounds of Parliament Hill in Ottawa.

narration.text: After December events, 73% supported the gilets jaunes, while 85% opposed Paris violence.
narration.quote: An opinion poll conducted after 1 December events found that 73 per cent of French people supported the gilets jaunes and that 85 per cent were opposed to the violence in Paris.

narration.text: The change was a factor in the rise of the yellow vest movement.
narration.quote: The change was opposed and was a factor in the rise of the yellow vest movement.

scenes.title: The record
scenes.purpose: Show what was written down, and what the writing left out.

narration.text: European leaders rarely backed anti-government protesters.
narration.quote: AFP reported that it is "extremely rare for European leaders to back anti-government protesters in a fellow member state".

narration.text: Tollbooths were blocked on 20 major arteries across France.
narration.quote: Vinci Autoroutes reported tollbooths were blocked on 20 major arteries all across France.

narration.text: Saint-Étienne was under siege during the protests.
narration.quote: On the same day, France Bleu reported that Saint-Étienne was "under siege".

narration.text: Around 106,000 people participated nationwide, including 24,000 in Paris.
narration.quote: Around 106,000 people took to the streets nationwide, including 24,000 in Paris, the interior ministry said, in the lowest turnout in recent weeks. ⬇️ FRANCE 24's Jamie Smith-Maillet reports from Paris.

narration.text: Demonstrations remained relatively calm compared to previous weekends.
narration.quote: Despite these incidents, the media reported that demonstrations "remained relatively calm compared to previous weekends".

narration.text: Violent but limited incidents marked Saturday's protest in France.
narration.quote: 14/11/2026 - 21:02 Authorities report violent but limited incidents across France Saturday's latest day of protests in France was marked by a decline in turnout, as well as violent but limited incidents in several cities, according to authorities.

narration.text: Police used explosive grenades and flashball weapons, causing injuries.
narration.quote: International media also reported on the disproportionate violence the French police deployed against the protestors, including the use of explosive grenades and flashball weapons resulting in multiple incidents of loss of limb and sight by the protestors.

narration.text: Yellow vests attacked journalists with verbal and physical violence.
narration.quote: Multiple verbal and physical attacks perpetrated by yellow vests against journalists have been reported and documented throughout the movement.

narration.text: Youth unions reported 200,000 protesters, including 100,000 in Paris.
narration.quote: Meanwhile, the youth inter-union coalition reported 200,000 protesters in France, including 100,000 in Paris, compared to 250,000 nationwide, including 75,000 in the capital, last Saturday.

narration.text: A library report documented social protest and discontent in France.
